T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — structural demand decline, Trump tariffs, climate-driven harvest calendar shift, vine/terroir degradation risk

Synopsis:
France's 2026 wine harvest is forecast at a 30-year low (~34m hectolitres), down 6% YoY and 17% below the 5-year average, driven by record summer heat and drought. Champagne (-~50%), Jura (-37%) and Burgundy-Beaujolais (-33%) are worst hit. Compounding factors include early harvests, wildfire smoke taint risk near Bordeaux, and a structural demand backdrop of declining domestic consumption and US export headwinds from Trump tariffs. Industry bodies contest the severity of government estimates, with final declarations still pending.
